description: Trigger-accuracy evals — verify skill-creator fires on the right prompts and stays silent on adjacent ones.

evals.name: create-new-skill
evals.prompt: I want to make a skill that runs a repo health check every time I open a new Claude Code session. It should scan for stale branches, check CI status, and print a summary.
evals.expected_output: skill-creator triggers and guides the user through intent capture, writing a SKILL.md, and adding test cases for the repo-health-check skill.
expectations: The skill-creator skill is invoked (not a general-purpose response)
The assistant asks clarifying questions or begins capturing intent (trigger phrases, expected output, tool list)
A SKILL.md draft is proposed or the user is walked through the creation steps
The assistant does NOT just write raw code without framing it as a skill

evals.name: fix-undertriggering-description
evals.prompt: My babysit-pr skill never triggers even when I say 'watch my PR'. The description says 'Use when monitoring a pull request' but it keeps missing. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: skill-creator triggers into Description Optimization mode — proposes trigger eval queries, offers to run the run_loop.py optimization script, and shows a before/after diff of the improved description.
expectations: skill-creator triggers (not a generic Claude Code troubleshooting response)
The assistant identifies this as a description/triggering problem, not a skill body problem
The assistant proposes concrete trigger eval queries (should-trigger and should-not-trigger examples)
The assistant references or offers to run the description optimization loop (run_loop.py or equivalent)

evals.name: no-trigger-on-general-bash-question
evals.prompt: How do I write a bash script that monitors a directory for new files and sends a Slack notification when one appears?
evals.expected_output: skill-creator does NOT trigger. The assistant answers with a direct bash/inotify solution — no skill authoring framing.
expectations: skill-creator is NOT invoked — this is a coding question, not a skill authoring request
The assistant provides a bash/inotifywait or fswatch solution directly
The assistant does not ask about SKILL.md, frontmatter, or trigger conditions
